pages.summary: The current folder, and changing it.
body: Files named without a folder are read and written in the current folder, and functions there are found before those on the path. `cd` with no input gives the current folder; `cd ..` goes up one.

examples.title: Into a folder and back
examples.code:
mkdir work
cd work
[~, here] = fileparts(pwd)
cd ..
isfolder('work')

body: `dir` lists a folder (or the files a pattern with `*` matches) with dates and sizes, or gives a struct array of name, folder, date, bytes, isdir and datenum; `ls` lists only the names; `what` the program files and MAT-files.

pages.summary: Where a function or file is found, and the text of a file.
body: `which` says whether a name is a built-in function, or where its file is on the path (the current folder first); with an output it gives that as text. `type` shows a file's text (a name without an extension looks for a program file).

examples.title: A built-in and a file of one's own
examples.output:
built-in (sqrt)
f =

    'twice'

e =

    '.m'


function y = twice(x)
y = 2*x;
end

pages.summary: Files opened in the Editor, opened by their kind, and scripts run.
body: `edit` opens a file in the Editor (a new script if it does not exist). `open` opens a file by its kind: program files in the Editor, MAT-files into the workspace (or a struct with an output), figure files as figures. `run` runs a script by its file name, from its own folder; it also runs test suites and global optimization searches.

examples.title: A script written and run, a MAT-file opened
examples.intro: Run in the page, `edit setup.m` opens the script in the Editor.
examples.output:
b =

     9

s = 

  struct with fields:

    c: [1 2 3]

pages.summary: Folders made and removed, and files deleted, copied and moved.
body: `mkdir` makes a folder (with the folders above it), saying so if it exists; `rmdir` removes an empty folder, or with `'s'` the folder and everything in it; `delete` deletes files (patterns with `*` too), and graphics objects. `copyfile` and `movefile` copy and move (or rename) files and folders. The functions give a status and a message when asked, instead of an error.
syntax: Made in a parent, with the result.

examples.title: A folder's life
examples.code:
mkdir('box/inner')
fclose(fopen('box/one.txt', 'w'));
copyfile('box/one.txt', 'box/two.txt')
movefile('box/two.txt', 'box/inner/three.txt')
ls box
ls box/inner
delete box/one.txt
rmdir('box', 's')
isfolder('box')

pages.summary: Archives: zip files, gzip files and tar files made and unpacked.
body: `zip` packs files and folders (names, a cell of names, or patterns) into a zip file, each entry named by its path from a root folder; `unzip` unpacks it, leaving out any entry that would land outside the folder. `gzip` compresses each file into a .gz file of its own and `gunzip` unpacks them. `tar` packs into a tar file, compressed when its name ends in .tgz or .tar.gz, and `untar` unpacks it. Each gives the names when asked.

pages.summary: Paths from their parts, and paths taken apart.
body: `fullfile` joins folders and a file name with the separator `/` (`filesep`), without doubling it; `fileparts` splits a path into its folder, name and extension (the last dot's). `pathsep` is the separator of the search path, `:`.

examples.title: Built and taken apart
examples.code:
p = fullfile('data', 'raw/', 'run1.csv')
[f, n, e] = fileparts(p)
[~, n2, e2] = fileparts('archive.tar.gz')
[filesep pathsep]
examples.output:

    'data/raw/run1.csv'

f =

    'data/raw'

n =

    'run1'

e =

    '.csv'

n2 =

    'archive.tar'

e2 =

ans =

pages.summary: Temporary names, and whether files and folders exist.
body: `tempdir` gives a folder for temporary files and `tempname` a name in it that no file has yet (made of random characters). `isfile` is true for a file that exists, `isfolder` for a folder (`isdir` is its older name); both take arrays of names.

examples.title: A scratch file that comes and goes
examples.code:
f = [tempname '.txt'];
isfile(f)
writelines("scratch", f);
isfile(f)
delete(f)
[isfolder(tempdir), isfile(tempdir), isdir(tempdir)]
isfolder(["." "no such folder"])

pages.summary: The search path: the folders where functions are looked for.
body: A function is looked for in the current folder, then in the folders of the path in order. `addpath` puts folders at the front (or with `'-end'` at the back), `rmpath` takes them off; `path` gives the path (or sets it); `genpath` gives a folder and every folder under it, ready for `addpath`. `rehash` looks again for program files, which here happens by itself whenever files change.
syntax: A folder and those under it.

examples.title: A function in a folder of its own
examples.code:
mkdir tools/more
fid = fopen('tools/more/thrice.m', 'w'); fprintf(fid, 'function y = thrice(x)\ny = 3*x;\nend\n'); fclose(fid);
exist('thrice')
addpath(genpath('tools'))
thrice(5)
rmpath(genpath('tools'))
exist('thrice')
numel(strsplit(genpath('tools'), pathsep))

pages.summary: A file's attributes, and whether deleted files go to a recycle bin.
body: `fileattrib` gives a file's or folder's attributes as a struct (read, write and execute for the user, group and others, whether it is a folder), or changes them by a mode such as `'+w'` or `'-x'`; a `*` in the name matches several. `recycle` says whether deleted files go to a recycle bin; there is none here, so `delete` removes files for good.
